title: Federal automated vehicle framework and deployment exemptions (policy-created opportunity)
sub_issue: automated driving systems deployment pathway (US federal)

business_activity.name: Autonomous vehicle partnerships offered on the Uber platform

policy_mechanism: Safety regulation and exemption pathway: AV framework updates and interim guidance on commercial deployment exemptions

mechanism_chain.text: NHTSA announced an AV framework designed to 'remove regulatory barriers' to ADS technologies and, in July 2026, requested comment on interim guidance for commercial deployment exemptions.
Uber discloses substantial investments in AV partners whose vehicles operate on its platform.

A clearer federal deployment-exemption path could expand where partner AVs can operate on Uber's network (market access); Uber also discloses the strategy may reduce the need for drivers, a workforce-relations exposure.

events.description: NHTSA notice: AV Framework Updates and request for comments on interim guidance (comments due Aug 31, 2026)
Uber FY2025 10-K discloses substantial AV partner investments and driver-dissatisfaction risk from its AV strategy

financial_linkage.detail: No separate AV revenue or investment quantum is disclosed in the 10-K risk factors reviewed.
financial_linkage.gap: AV economics are undisclosed; any scale estimate would be a proxy and is therefore not made.

rationale: Kept on the emerging list: the federal signal is a framework plus a request for comment, not a binding rule, so process status is Agenda. Included deliberately as a policy-created opportunity, per the paper's symmetric dependency/opportunity detector. Confidence is Medium because the business-effect chain is inferred rather than stated by either source.
gaps: Exemption application outcomes and state AV rules are not covered by the connectors in this build.
Whether Uber's AV partners would seek exemptions is not established by any retrieved source.
